h1: The 8 Best Robot Vacuum and Mop Combos of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Robot Vacuum and Mop Combos: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 robot vacuum and mop combos, from roborock and eufy docks to a budget Tikom, scored on mopping, docks and value.
summary: The roborock Qrevo S5V is the combo to buy if mopping quality matters, because its FlexiArm reaches edges that fixed pads miss. The eufy Omni C20 is the pick for a dock that empties the bin, washes the pads and refills the tank. The iRobot Roomba 105 Combo suits buyers who want LiDAR mapping and a 75 day AutoEmpty dock. On a tight budget, the roborock Q7 L5 gives the best suction for the money.
intro: A combo robot has to be good at two jobs that pull against each other. Suction wants a heavy, dry brush. Mopping wants a damp pad that stays off carpet. Most cheap combos do both jobs adequately and neither well, and the dock is where a good one separates from a mediocre one.

We reviewed eight combos, spread from under $150 to about $500, and ranked them on how the listings describe mopping, what the dock does without your help, and how much suction you get for the price. Rankings come from spec sheets and owner-reported behavior, not from running the machines ourselves.

products.name: roborock Qrevo S5V Robot Vacuum and Mop, FlexiArm Edge Mopping
products.verdict: FlexiArm edge mopping reaches corners and baseboards that a fixed pad skips.
products.description:
The Qrevo S5V is a premium vacuum and mop combo with FlexiArm edge mopping and what the listing calls premium navigation. The arm extends a mop pad toward edges, which addresses the biggest mopping complaint: dirty corners and baseboards.

It takes first place over the eufy Omni C20 because mopping reach is the thing buyers feel most. The Omni's dock is more automated in the listing, but a robot that leaves the edges dirty needs you to do the work anyway. The cost is a price near the top of the roundup.

Buy it if you have hard floors with plenty of baseboards. Caveat: the listing gives no suction number to compare.
cons: Near the top of the price range
products.idealFor: Hard-floor homes with lots of baseboards and corners.
products.skipIf: You are working to a tight budget.

products.name: eufy Omni C20 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo for Hardwood and Carpet
products.verdict: A dock that empties the bin, washes the pads and refills the water.
products.description:
The Omni C20 is built around an all-in-one dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop pads and refills the tank, and the robot is rated for hardwood and carpet. That dock removes the three chores that most combos leave you.

It ranks second behind the Qrevo S5V because mopping reach counts for more than dock automation, but it beats the Roomba 105 Combo by washing its own pads. At a mid-range price it is the best value among the docked models.

Best for busy households that want to touch the machine as little as possible. Caveat: the listing gives no suction figure.
pros: Mid-range price for a full dock
products.skipIf: You have no room for a large dock.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 105 Combo Robot Vacuum & Mop with AutoEmpty Dock
products.verdict: LiDAR navigation and a dock that empties itself for up to 75 days.
products.description:
The Roomba 105 Combo pairs LiDAR navigation, power-lifting suction and multiple cleaning modes with an AutoEmpty dock rated for up to 75 days. The listing sells it on consistent mapping and long periods between bin chores.

It sits third because the dock empties but, unlike the Eufy Omni C20, does not wash the pads. Against the Q10 S5+, you pay a bit more for LiDAR and iRobot's long dock window.

Best for buyers who value mapping and a dock that disappears for weeks. Caveat: for mopping detail, the listing is quieter than the roborock Qrevo S5V.
products.idealFor: Mapping fans who want a long dock interval.
products.skipIf: You want the dock to wash the pads for you.

products.name: eufy C28 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 15,000 Pa, HydroJet Roller Mop
products.verdict: The highest suction here, 15,000 Pa, with a HydroJet roller mop.
products.description:
The C28 lists 15,000 Pa suction, the highest in this ranking, with a HydroJet roller mop instead of a flat pad. That suction rating matters on thicker carpet, where lower-powered combos struggle.

It ranks fourth because it costs about as much as the Qrevo S5V without the edge arm, and the listing names no dock. Compared with the Q10 S5+, you pay a lot more for suction and the roller mop.

Good for mixed carpet and hard floor homes. Caveat: the sticker price sits near the top of the range.
products.idealFor: Mixed carpet and hard floor homes.
products.skipIf: Edge mopping is your main concern.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: 10,000Pa, a self-empty dock and a mop for under $300.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ lists 10,000Pa suction, a self-empty dock and a mop function. For under $300, it puts a dock in a price bracket where most combos have none.

It ranks fifth because the models above add LiDAR, edge mopping or washing docks. It beats the Q7 L5 by adding the dock and 2,000 more Pa.

Best for a mid-budget buyer who wants a dock. Caveat: the listing gives little detail on mopping.
products.idealFor: Mid-budget buyers who want a dock.

products.name: roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 8,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: 8,000Pa from a known brand, at the price of a budget unit.
products.description:
The Q7 L5 brings a rated 8,000Pa of suction and a mop to a price around $140. It is the stronger suction-per-dollar choice among the budget combos here.

It ranks sixth because it has no dock listed, and the models above add one. Against the ROPVACNIC below, you pay about the same and get the better known name.

For small homes where cost matters most. Caveat: expect manual bin emptying.
products.idealFor: Small homes on a strict budget.

products.name: ROPVACNIC Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo 5200Pa Suction Robotic Cleaner
products.verdict: 5200Pa and a compact body in the same tier as the Tikom.
products.description:
The ROPVACNIC lists 5200Pa suction, a vacuum and mop design and a compact body. It competes directly with the Tikom G8000 Max on price and edges it on suction.

It ranks seventh because the Roborock Q7 L5 costs about the same with 8,000Pa and a stronger brand. Compared with the Tikom, it gives a small suction bump but no runtime figure.

Consider it for a small apartment. Caveat: the brand is lesser known, so support is a gamble.

products.name: Tikom Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 5000Pa, 150 Min Max (G8000 Max)
products.verdict: The least expensive combo here, with app, remote and 150 minutes of runtime.
products.description:
The G8000 Max lists 5000Pa suction, 150 minutes of runtime and app plus remote control. At under $150 it is the least expensive combo in this ranking and still covers the basics.

It ranks last because 5000Pa is the lowest figure here and no dock is listed. The ROPVACNIC edges it on suction, but the Tikom is the one with a stated runtime.

Pick it for a small home where a combo is a nice to have. Caveat: do not expect much on thick carpet.
products.idealFor: Small homes with mostly hard floor.

whatMatters.factor: Edges decide how clean the floor looks
whatMatters.detail: A round or square pad leaves a gap along baseboards and in corners, which is the first thing you notice on a clean floor. Features such as an extending arm or a roller help. Check the listing for edge or corner mopping, and look at owner photos of baseboards.

A basic dock only charges. A better one empties the bin, a premium one also washes the pads and refills the tank. Count how many of those you would do by hand each week, and weigh that against the extra cost.
A wet pad on carpet leaves damp spots. Look for pad lifting or carpet detection in the listing, or plan to set no-mop zones in the app.
Pa is a pressure rating, and each brand measures it in its own way, usually at peak. Use it for comparing models in the same brand. Anything near 8,000Pa is fine for hard floors and low-pile rugs.

whatMatters.factor: Water tank size sets your coverage
whatMatters.detail: A small tank runs dry before a large home is done. Find the tank capacity in the specs and compare it to your square footage, or choose a model with a dock that refills.

faq.q: Do combo robots mop as well as a separate mop?
faq.a: Not quite. They damp-wipe and keep light dirt under control, but sticky spills still need a manual pass. Models with an edge arm like the Qrevo S5V come closer.

faq.q: Can a combo robot go on carpet?
faq.a: Yes, if it lifts its pad or detects carpet. Check the listing, because without that the pad can leave damp spots.

faq.q: Is the eufy Omni C20 worth more than the Q10 S5+?
faq.a: If you hate chores, yes: the Omni's dock empties, washes and refills. The Q10 S5+ only empties the bin.

faq.q: How often do I need to wash the pads?
faq.a: After every run on a basic dock. A washing dock like the Omni C20 does it for you.
About 5,000Pa is fine for hard floors. For carpet, aim for 8,000Pa or more, as on the Q7 L5 and the C28.
It helps with room mapping and dark rooms. The Roomba 105 Combo is the LiDAR option here, and budget models use simpler navigation.

finalTake: For most buyers who want clean floors, the roborock Qrevo S5V is the best combo here because its edge arm solves the worst mopping complaint. The eufy Omni C20 is the answer for anyone who wants a dock that does the chores. On a budget, the roborock Q7 L5 offers the best suction per dollar, and the Tikom is the cheapest way in.
